interface.name: picowl_rotation_manager_v1

description.summary: how an output is turned, also by the display

interface.description: With hardware rotation the display turns the picture, so wl_output tells clients the transform normal and an output that is physically turned looks like an unturned one with swapped sides. A client that cares where the physical top of the device is (a status bar that belongs on the short edge of a portrait panel) asks here. Nothing about wl_output changes; a client that does not bind this sees what it saw before.

request.name: get_rotation

description.summary: get the rotation of an output

request.description: The picowl_rotation_v1 sends its first rotation event at once and another one whenever the rotation, who does it or the native subpixel layout of the output changes.

interface.name: picowl_rotation_v1
interface.description: Sent for the output of the wl_output given to get_rotation. The wl_output of a removed output gets no events.

event.name: rotation
event.description:
transform is the wl_output.transform value that turns the panel as it is built (its native orientation) into what the user sees: with software rotation the one wl_output.geometry carries, with hardware rotation what that event leaves out. hardware is 1 when the display does the turning, 0 when the compositor does (then wl_output.geometry says the same and this event adds nothing).
subpixel is the wl_output.subpixel value of the panel in its native orientation, whatever the rotation. wl_output.geometry carries it that way with software rotation and as the client sees it with hardware rotation; this is the one that applies to anything drawn in the panel's own orientation and turned by a buffer transform.
